sections.html:
Murfreesboro is the Rutherford County seat, about 34 miles from downtown Nashville, to the southeast. It had 171,178 residents by mid-2025, up from 152,769 in 2020. A sale touches three separate offices: the city's Tax Department, the Rutherford County Assessor and the county Register of Deeds.

A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $402,100, and typical gross rent is $1,481 a month. Owners occupy 52.4 percent of homes, so almost half are rented or empty. Mention tenants to a buyer early. City-wide medians are a rough guide, and recent closed sales on your own street are a better one.

Bills for 2026 went out on October 1, 2026. The city charges no interest if payment arrives by February 28, 2027, and the same February 28 deadline applies every year from tax year 2025 forward. After that, March 1 starts a charge of 1.5 percent per month or fraction on the base tax. Your postmark counts as the payment date, and if the 28th falls on a weekend, you have until the next business day.

Ways to pay the Murfreesboro city bill
Payment methodWhereCost or hours
Onlinemurfreesborotntax.comCard, PayPal or e-check; card fees about 2.5 percent plus $0.30, e-check $1.50
MailCity of Murfreesboro, P.O. Box 1139, Murfreesboro, TN 37133-1139Postmark accepted
In personCity Hall Finance Department, first floor, 111 West Vine Street8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. weekdays

You may pay in part if you follow the city's guidelines. Whatever stays unpaid is sent to Chancery Court at the proper deadline. The City Tax Department's number is (615) 893-5210.

Values come from the Rutherford County Assessor's Office, (615) 898-7750, and the city bills on those values. Tennessee law sets residential assessments at 25 percent of appraised value. The county board of equalization starts meeting each June 1; call the assessor to learn the current filing cutoff.

Murfreesboro participates in the state's Property Tax Freeze and Property Tax Relief programs, which serve low-income seniors 65 and older and qualifying disabled owners. Enrolled in one? Ask the City Tax Department what a sale does to your application before listing.

An unpaid bill will not stop a closing. Your title company requests a payoff figure from the City Tax Department and takes the balance out of the sale money. A balance already sent to Chancery Court is different: say so immediately, because it changes who gets paid and on what timeline.

Building and Codes applies the 2024 building codes to plan review, inspections and certificates of occupancy. Inspectors take questions at the office early each morning before they head to job sites, and the front counter stops taking money at 4:00 p.m. The City Council also keeps a schedule of development impact fees, which matters mainly if you remodel or add on before selling, so ask the office what applies to your project.

Hosting guests means a 5 percent occupancy tax paid monthly to the county and city, plus state business and sales tax. Airbnb and VRBO hosts are included. Each host needs two $15 business licenses, one from the county clerk and one from the city. Pass the license records to your buyer.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Rutherford County
sections.html:
The recording office is Room 133 at 319 North Maple Street. The office's posted policy keeps an overage of $10 or less, refunds larger overpayments by check at month's end and sends back any document that arrives short on fees the same day.

Tennessee's transfer tax, 37 cents per $100, is paid at recording by the buyer as grantee.

On April 10, 2009, a low-end EF4 tornado struck the fringes of the city, killing two people and injuring 41. It destroyed 117 homes and heavily damaged 292. Storm history can come up with buyers in older neighborhoods. After any roof replacement or storm rebuild, keep the invoices and permit numbers in one folder.

Rentals fill a large share of Murfreesboro, and a buyer who learns a tenant is in place will want the lease, the monthly rent and the end date. Investors also measure your price against the $1,481 rent figure.

A tenant who is leaving should be named with a date. A firm move-out date makes a closing simpler than an open-ended lease does.

• Your latest city tax statement and a payoff from the City Tax Department.
  • Your deed and a plain list of any liens or mortgage balances.
  • Permit numbers and invoices for roof, storm or other major work.
  • Lease and rent details for any tenant.
  • Short-term rental licenses, if guests have stayed in the house.

The county Assessor's phone number and the Register's address are worth writing down too, since a title agent may send you to either.

sections.h2: Listing or cash: how to decide
sections.html:
Listing puts the house in front of the most buyers and can earn the best price, along with open houses, an appraisal and a repair list. A cash sale narrows the audience but gives you a faster, steadier closing. Either way the same three offices collect what they are owed.

Rapid growth tends to help a house in good condition. A house needing work may lose more to repair time and cost than a higher list price would add.

sections.h2: Who to call before you list
sections.html:
• City Tax Department, (615) 893-5210, for the city balance and payment questions.
  • Rutherford County Assessor, (615) 898-7750, for your appraised value and appeal timing.
  • Building and Codes, for permit history and certificates of occupancy.
  • Register of Deeds, Room 133 at 319 North Maple Street, for recording questions.

Make these calls a couple of weeks before a planned closing. Problems found early, such as an old permit or a balance you forgot, are cheap to fix. The same problems found at the table can push the date back and cost you the buyer.

1. Describe the property and mention tenants.
  2. A buyer sends an offer, and you accept it.
  3. Your title company requests the city payoff and reviews county records.
  4. The deed is signed, the transfer tax is paid and the document is recorded on North Maple Street.
  5. Taxes owed and any mortgage payoff are deducted from your share.

Without a lender, the date depends on title work rather than a bank appraisal, which suits a fixed moving date or a vacant rental.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Murfreesboro city taxes?
faqs.a: Right after February 28. For tax year 2026 that means March 1, 2027, and the charge is 1.5 percent for each month or fraction on the base amount. A deadline falling on a weekend moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I pay Murfreesboro city taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Partial payments are allowed if you follow the guidelines. Anything left unpaid is turned over to Chancery Court at the proper deadline, so call (615) 893-5210 first.
Start with the county Assessor's Office, (615) 898-7750. For paying the bill or applying for relief, use the City Tax Department, (615) 893-5210.

faqs.q: Is there property tax help for seniors in Murfreesboro?
faqs.a: Yes. The city participates in Tennessee's Property Tax Freeze and Property Tax Relief programs for qualifying low-income owners 65 and older and for qualifying disabled owners.

faqs.q: What do short-term rental owners owe in Murfreesboro?
faqs.a: A 5 percent occupancy tax paid monthly to the county and city, state sales tax and gross receipts business tax, and $15 business licenses from the county clerk and the city.
